tier_reason: Independent run (by the pillow-lunasvg author, not LunaSVG's author sammycage) with a public harness (benchmarks/bench.py: min of 3 interleaved runs per file, median over pinned corpora), stated hardware (Apple M4), library versions and corpus commits; every number in the record matches benchmarks/results.md. Not A: no compiler or flags are stated and the repo's CMakeLists.txt/pyproject.toml set no build type or optimization flags.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Median ms per file, SVG bytes to PNG bytes (benchmarks/results.md): simple-icons at 256 px pillow-lunasvg 1.00 vs cairosvg 2.17 and resvg-py 2.84 (README: 2.2x and 2.8x faster); at 1024 px 12.56 vs 23.63 and 34.85 (README: 1.9x and 2.8x). Render only, without PNG encode: 0.11 ms at 256 px and 0.88 ms at 1024 px. resvg feature tests (filters and text not timed): 256 px 0.45 vs 1.47 cairosvg and 2.17 resvg-py; 1024 px 5.26 vs 19.16 cairosvg and 27.22 resvg-py, over 943, 884 and 941 files respectively because files a renderer rejected are dropped from its median.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: pillow-lunasvg 0.1.0 built locally from commit 653c187 (LunaSVG 3.5.0) via pip with scikit-build-core and CMake; CMakeLists.txt sets only C++17, static lunasvg/plutovg and LUNASVG_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_RESOURCES, with no CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE or optimization flags, so the build tool's default applies; compiler and version not stated (macOS host). Python 3.13.15, Pillow 12.3.0, resvg-py 0.5.0, cairosvg 2.9.1 with cairo 1.18.4 from Homebrew. Exact commands are in results.md.
corrections.caveats: Measured by the author of the pillow-lunasvg wrapper (independent of LunaSVG's author, but promoting his own wrapper; he added pillow-lunasvg to LunaSVG's README via PR #273, merged 2026-09-17). The benchmark repo has 0 stars and 15 commits. The pipeline is timed through Python: about 89% of pillow-lunasvg's 1.00 ms is Pillow load plus PNG encode (render only 0.11 ms), and the three tools use different PNG encoders (Pillow zlib, cairo's PNG writer, resvg's encoder), while cairosvg parses SVG in Python, so the gap over cairosvg reflects front-end and encoder overhead more than Cairo's rasterizer versus plutovg. On the resvg test corpus LunaSVG does less work: it lacks filters, the CSS transform property, transform-origin, mix-blend-mode, context-fill and SVG/WebP inside <image> (59% loose fidelity match against resvg), and per-renderer medians cover different file subsets. Filter tests are not timed. On simple-icons fidelity is comparable (99.0% vs cairosvg 99.4% strict). The machine was not idle during the run (another development session), which is why min-of-3 was used. Baselines are Python packages (cairosvg, resvg-py), not the category's C/C++ incumbents.

notes: Numbers verified line by line against results.md and the timing code in bench.py. Keep at B as independent measurement, but the measurer has an interest in the wrapper, so the orchestrator may prefer C under the vendor-evidence precedent. LunaSVG metadata checked: MIT, 1.2k stars, last commit 2026-09-17, not archived.

tier_reason: First-party README chart with public Google Benchmark code (tests/benchmarks/RenderPerfBench.cpp, run_render_perf_compare.sh) and flags readable from bazel/defs.bzl, but no compiler version, no CPU models and no published result files, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: up to 1.9x faster than Rust tiny-skia at 512x512, normalized to Rust = 1.0x: FillRect 1.9x ARM (NEON) and 1.3x x86 (AVX2+FMA); FillPath 1.4x ARM and 1.2x x86; C++ SIMD over C++ scalar up to 2.3x (x86) and 1.9x (ARM). The x86 ratios compare an AVX2+FMA C++ build with a Rust build that has no AVX enabled. The regression test's calibrated baselines (tests/benchmarks/run_render_perf_regression_test.sh) match the README on x86 (simd_over_rust 1.18 FillPath, 1.29 FillRect) but not on arm64 (simd_over_rust 2.90 FillPath and 3.50 FillRect; simd_over_scalar 2.80 and 3.90), so the README's ARM figures and the calibration disagree. No raw result files are published.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Bazel -c opt. C++ library copts: -std=c++20 -ffp-contract=off -Wall -O3, plus -mavx2 -mfma for the native x86 build (bazel/defs.bzl); host C++ compiler and version not stated (CONTRIBUTING lists GCC 11+, Clang 14+ or MSVC 19.30+ as supported). Rust tiny-skia 0.12.0 is built through rules_rust 0.71.3 as a rust_static_library with no rustc target-cpu or target-feature flags (tests/rust_ffi/BUILD.bazel, MODULE.bazel), so it runs SSE2 code on x86-64; tiny-skia's README says AVX needs -Ctarget-cpu=haswell. Google Benchmark 1.9.5: 5 repetitions, min_time 0.2 s, mean real time; the Rust time is the average of its runs in the native and scalar binaries.
corrections.caveats: C++ port of linebender/tiny-skia, benchmarked only against its own Rust original, not against Skia, Cairo or Blend2D. On x86 the comparison is unequal: the C++ side is compiled with -mavx2 -mfma, the Rust side without AVX. On FillPath the two sides run different anti-aliasing algorithms: the C++ port fills anti-aliased paths with analytic AA (src/tiny_skia/scan/PathAa.cpp, ported from Skia's SkScan_AAAPath.cpp), which the README names as one reason its output is not bit-exact with Rust tiny-skia. The README's ARM ratios disagree with the arm64 baselines in the regression test (2.90x and 3.50x). Only two workloads at one size; CPU models and compiler versions not stated. Rust tiny-skia's README says it is 20-100% slower than Skia on x86-64 and 100-300% slower on ARM, so a 1.2-1.9x gain over it does not show the port beats Skia (inference). 9 stars, 156 commits; the latest commits (2026-07-04) are mostly renovate[bot] dependency bumps alongside one author commit.

notes: Possible duplicate or port: the baseline is the project's own original, linebender/tiny-skia, which wave 10 batch-03 already confirmed at tier A; the orchestrator may want decision duplicate, or keep it as the C++ form of that entry. Numbers on the README match the record, but the x86 build is ISA-mismatched and the ARM figures conflict with the repo's own calibrated regression baselines. Metadata checked: BSD-3-Clause, 9 stars, last commit 2026-07-04, not a fork.

tier_reason: First-party chart (vgperf.png, embedded in both READMEs) produced by the author's public harness (vgperf src/main.c, src/vkvg, src/cairo, src/skia). No GPU or CPU model, vkvg or Cairo build flags, versions or harness options are stated, and no numeric results file exists, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Chart only. Per vgperf src/main.c the bars are median wall-clock seconds per iteration (gettimeofday, lower is better; each iteration draws opt.count shapes, default 100, on a default 512x512 surface; the options used for the chart are not stated). Approximate readings from the PNG: lines stroke vkvg ~0.00013, cairo es3 ~0.0031, skia ~0.0004; rectangles ~0.00026, ~0.00026, ~0.00022; circles ~0.00065, ~0.0035, ~0.00016; stars ~0.00058, ~0.0019, ~0.00062. So vkvg is about 24x, 5x and 3x faster than Cairo GL ES3 on lines, circles and stars and ties on rectangles; against Skia Vulkan it is about 3x faster on lines, roughly ties on stars, is slightly slower on rectangles and about 4x slower on circles (derived from page data).
corrections.workload: vgperf, a caskbench-style C harness, timing four tests (lines stroke, rectangles, circles, stars) with vkvg (Vulkan), Cairo (GL ES3/EGL surface) and Skia (Vulkan backend via a patched experimental C API); each timed iteration draws a batch of random shapes and, when on-screen presentation is enabled, flushes and presents the surface.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Skia built with gn args is_official_build=true is_component_build=true skia_use_vulkan=true (vgperf README); vgperf's own CMakeLists.txt defaults to a Debug build when no build type is given (harness driver only); vkvg and Cairo builds, compilers and flags not stated.
corrections.caveats: First-party chart with no axis label, unit, GPU or CPU model, run count or Cairo/vkvg versions; the unit (median seconds per iteration) is inferred from vgperf src/main.c. The chart was last updated on 2022-01-19 (vgperf commit 'update perf chart with latest vkvg'), so it predates more than four years of vkvg changes. vgperf (5 stars, 22 commits, MIT) has no numeric results, only the chart. Cairo is measured through its GL ES3 backend, not its default image (CPU) backend; Skia was built from a patched experimental C API branch. Only 4 simple drawing tests. Mixed result against Skia: clearly slower on circles, slightly slower on rectangles.

notes: Chart readings in the record are accurate apart from stars versus Skia, which is a near tie rather than a loss; ratios now labelled as derived. Harness code was read: vkvg's timed present path calls vkvg_flush, which in current vkvg source waits for the flush fence, while vkDeviceWaitIdle is commented out. Metadata checked: MIT, 819 stars, last commit 2026-10-01, not archived.
